To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) EBM sampling trajectories of different magnitudes correspond to different learning objectives; and 2) MCMC initialization strategies can be leveraged to improve the performance of EBMs for each of these objectives.

(i) EBM sampling trajectories of different lengths can be learned from the same model architecture with the same objective function, (ii) the length of a sampling trajectory is determined by the initialization strategy used to learn an EBM, (iii) the best initialization strategy for a given sampling trajectory length is not necessarily the best for other trajectory lengths, (iv) the best initialization strategies for shortrun sampling are different than those for longrun sampling, (v) shortrun sampling can be used for

1) the choice of MCMC sampling trajectory length is critical for learning EBMs with desired performance; 2) the initialization of the negative samples used for ML learning is critical for learning high-quality EBMs with desired sampling performance; and 3), our novel MCMC initialization strategies are effective across a wide range of MCMC trajectory lengths and learning outcomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: How should an EBM be learned to achieve different sampling outcomes?
the MCMC lifecycle of an EBM: how to initialize MCMC trajectories for ML learning and how to use these trajectories in applications.
the question: How can we learn an EBM with different MCMC sampling properties for different purposes?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed methods are able to significantly improve the performance of EBMs in a range of tasks and applications.
the EBM framework is a powerful, general-purpose tool for learning and sampling complex probability densities, and that MCMC sampling can be leveraged to achieve a variety of learning outcomes.
MCMC sampling is a powerful and underutilized tool for learning EBMs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a new perspective for EBM learning and demonstrate that MCMC initialization is a critical component for learning high-quality EBMs.
MCMC initialization is an effective tool for learning EBM models for different purposes.
MCMC trajectories with different length can be learned with the same EBM, by initializing the MCMC sampling differently.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the length of MCMC sampling can be used as a knob for learning models that are tailored to specific downstream applications.
MCMC trajectories are not just a means to sample images, but also a tool to control the length of an EBM's training trajectory, and hence the model's learning outcome.
MCMC initialization is a powerful tool for learning EBM models with a variety of purposes.
